signs.name: Solid perception
signs.gloss: all images revolve around a central and privileged image
signs.difference: One body owns the frame: either we see through its eyes (POV, eyelid/mask/windscreen framing) or we see it held at the hub with everything else arranged around it — and the image would lose its organising centre if that body were removed.
signs.question: Whose world is this?

family.title: Indisch allerlei
family.note: Binocular mask: a distant ship held as the object of one gaze.
family.flip: the ship shrinks to a speck in a vast sea: the gaze reveals its own smallness

family.title: The House I Live In
family.note: Rifle-scope crosshair: the world arrives already centred on one eye.
family.flip: a counter-shot shows the target aiming back: the crosshair becomes one pole of a duel

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part I)
family.note: Peephole vignette: the frame becomes a single perceiver's aperture.
family.flip: the watcher's purpose (spy or guardian) becomes the question: one look, two situations

family.title: 6 1/2 Magic Hours
family.note: Through the windscreen: the road is organised around the driver's seat.
family.flip: the car's movement, not the driver's seat, organises the frame: the centre begins to flow

family.title: Winter in Den haag / IJs in Den Haag
family.note: Looking down at one's own skates: the perceiver's body enters its own view.
family.flip: the glide carries the view rather than a subject owning it

family.title: Eyes and Their Care (An Introduction), The
family.note: Eyes looking into the lens: the reverse shot that names the perceiving centre.
family.flip: the face stops being the one who sees and becomes the surface that is seen

signs.name: Liquid perception
signs.gloss: the flow from character/event to character/event
signs.difference: The centre moves: in a continuous reframing the shot passes from one character or environment to another, each central only until the next captures the screen.
signs.question: Does perception migrate?

family.title: Straight Talk
family.note: Following walkers into a crowd: perception passes from body to body.
family.flip: the camera locks onto one walker's back and the centre solidifies

family.title: Episode 19 - The Soil Explorers
family.note: Water-level view of a wake: vision carried on liquid movement.
family.flip: the water's flicker takes over and no vessel or viewer anchors it

family.title: A Poem in Marble, A Place on the Map: Byron R. White U.S. Courthouse, Denver, CO
family.note: Corridor tracking shot: the centre travels, handed from space to space.
family.flip: the corridor empties of any destination: space for its own sake

family.title: The National Wildlife Refuges of Alaska
family.note: A boat drifting midstream: the camera floats with the current, not a subject.
family.flip: the passengers become the fixed centre from which the river is seen

family.title: Master Hands (Part IV)
family.note: Drifting over a factory floor: the view slides across many workers' stations.
family.flip: the drift settles into an establishing survey of a determinate workplace

family.title: The Fed Today
family.note: A street crowd flowing past the lens: no one holds the frame for long.
family.flip: the crowd shares one affect (faces turned, a common expression)

signs.name: Gaseous perception
signs.gloss: all images resonate with one another as an acentred system
signs.difference: Nothing is privileged: through slow/fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation or micro-shooting the image treats a human figure as one image like any other among landscapes, matter and machines.
signs.question: Can the world perceive without a human center?

family.title: Photography
family.note: Microscopy: matter seen from no human scale.
family.flip: the cell reads as the seed of an environment to come

family.title: Fitting Faces
family.note: A field of lenses or bubbles: each image varies with every other.
family.flip: the multiplied discs reflect one actual image: mirrors face to face

family.title: Water
family.note: Light breaking on water: an acentred field of flickers.
family.flip: the flow carries a centre along (a boat, a swimmer)

family.title: Fashion's Favorite (Part I)
family.note: A macro lattice of fibres: pattern without a subject.
family.flip: the pattern has to be deciphered as something else

family.title: Amateur Film Medicus09a
family.note: Surf on a shore: waves acting on one another with no one watching.
family.flip: the shot is held for a watcher who cannot act on what they see

family.title: Telephone and Telegraph
family.note: Banks of relays: the machine registers signals with no operator.
family.flip: the rows read as a habitual series whose units matter

signs.name: Icon
signs.gloss: the face expressing unfilmable internal intensities
signs.difference: The face is not a feature of a person in a space but the whole image: a close-up in which expression (fixed wonder or traversing micro-movements) holds an intensity that has not yet become action.
signs.question: Where does intensity become a face?

family.title: Story of Television
family.note: Eyes shut, cheek lit: a face turned inward, an icon of quality.
family.flip: we can no longer tell whether she is falling into a dream

family.title: Place to Live, A
family.note: A boy's face fills the frame: wonder held before any action.
family.flip: a reverse shot makes him the one whose view organises the world

family.title: Eyes and Their Care (An Introduction), The
family.note: An upturned child's face in tight close-up: the face as reflecting surface.
family.flip: the face is only a seer before a situation it cannot answer

family.title: Coney Island - Food (Standard 4:3)
family.note: A woman's face half in shadow: expression with no motor outlet.
family.flip: the expression is seized by a drive about to break out

family.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHER
family.note: A weathered old face: a lifetime of qualities written as surface.
family.flip: the lines read as the world's imprint driving a coming action

family.title: Episode 10 - The EFNEP Program
family.note: A woman's pained face: a power rising (icon of power).
family.flip: the pain becomes a primal force acting through the body

signs.name: Dividual
signs.gloss: the conjunction of collective and individual affects
signs.difference: The feeling belongs to the gathering: the crowd, pack or series of faces is individualised as one affect while each person in it is de-individualised.
signs.question: Is the feeling mine, ours, or both?

family.title: Coney Island
family.note: A packed beach crowd: a mass in which faces stay legible.
family.flip: the crowd is only the setting for someone else's action

family.title: Unique Contribution, The (Part II)
family.note: A flock moving as one body, each animal still distinct.
family.flip: individuals dissolve into pure pattern

family.title: Space Ship Takeoff, a Technical Fantasy
family.note: An audience facing one screen: one affect spread across the seats.
family.flip: the screen they face matters more than their shared attention

family.title: Look to Lockheed for Leadership (Part I)
family.note: A shift crowd streaming through the gates: individual gaits inside one flow.
family.flip: individuals scatter onto separate trajectories

family.title: Winter in Den haag / IJs in Den Haag
family.note: Onlookers huddled in winter: a collective stance.
family.flip: the posture of waiting, not a shared affect, is what we see

family.title: Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: Birds lifting together: one gesture made by thousands.
family.flip: no single bird stays legible within the flock

signs.name: Any-space-whatever
signs.gloss: the expression of non-human affects
signs.difference: Affect with no face: an emptied, disconnected or amorphous space (fog, rain, shadow, coloured void, ruin, haze) that expresses a quality itself rather than locating an action.
signs.question: Has place stopped functioning as ordinary geography?

family.title: Old Time Tractor Plowing Dry Land
family.note: A field in fog: space as pure grey potential.
family.flip: the fog is framed as the threshold of a dream

family.title: Dust Storm
family.note: A dust storm whites out the land: space without coordinates.
family.flip: a watcher is shown unable to act before it: the space becomes an opsign

family.title: Shock Troops of Disaster: The Story of the New England Hurricane
family.note: Dark water in a flooded street at night: geography turned amorphous.
family.flip: the water reads as an elemental force in the city's depths

family.title: American Road, The (Part III)
family.note: A sun flare swallows the road: light dissolves the place.
family.flip: the light becomes a field of interacting particles

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 1
family.note: Earthquake rubble, no one in sight: a disconnected space.
family.flip: the ruin reads as primal force unleashed rather than space emptied out

family.title: Berlin: Symphony of a Great City
family.note: An empty station under a canopy: a transit space emptied of use.
family.flip: trains and passengers arrive: the station becomes a determinate milieu

signs.name: Symptom
signs.gloss: characters overwhelmed by primal forces
signs.difference: The body acts from a drive too strong for it: a visible primordial act (devouring, rutting, seizing, cruelty) in which the human behaves as a human animal, not as an agent with a goal.
signs.question: What force is acting through this body?

family.title: The National Wildlife Refuges of Alaska
family.note: An animal tearing at raw meat: drive with no mediation, the impulse too strong for the body.
family.flip: the meat, not the animal, becomes the charged object (Deamer's 'haunch of meat')

family.title: Nature's Cameo: Bryce Canyon National Park
family.note: Animals fighting in snow: primal force breaking through the milieu.
family.flip: the fight reads as a duel between two poles of a world

family.title: Valley Town
family.note: A hunched man eating: need takes over posture.
family.flip: the meal is simply daily life, patiently held

family.title: Robinson Crusoe B
family.note: A fur-clad castaway: a body returned to the animal.
family.flip: the figure is the emblem of a primal world rather than a body seized by its drive

family.title: Inside the Fed
family.note: Hands grabbing across a counter: appetite in the gesture.
family.flip: the grabbing is ordinary commerce in a workplace

family.title: Best Food In Town
family.note: Food taken from the plate: the partial object of hunger.
family.flip: the food as object carries the charge, not the eater

signs.name: Fetish
signs.gloss: a special object charged with primal energies, awaiting a grounding
signs.difference: A partial object is held apart and charged — relic or vult — so that the image makes us feel stored primal force in it, waiting for a body to discharge it.
signs.question: What object has become charged?

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part I)
family.note: A carved figure lit alone: an object holding primal power.
family.flip: the figure expresses an idea or belief instead of storing primal energy

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 5) (Part I)
family.note: An object glowing red in the dark: stored energy.
family.flip: the glow is the milieu's elemental fire rather than a single object

family.title: Speech: Platform Posture and Appearance
family.note: A pair of shoes isolated at floor level: Deamer's list includes the shoe.
family.flip: the shoes stand for a concept (status, a journey) rather than a drive

family.title: Verkade's fabrieken te Zaandam
family.note: A hand turning a small object under a lamp: the partial object handled.
family.flip: the handling is an investigation that discloses a situation

family.title: Laboratory Design for Microbiological Safety
family.note: An empty glass display case: the reliquary awaiting its charge.
family.flip: the case signifies an institution (museum, value), not a charge

signs.name: Originary world
signs.gloss: a universe of primal forces
signs.difference: Beneath a recognisable place rumbles an archetypal one: the forest, desert, swamp or house is shown as a determinate but timeless ground of drives and decay, not as a historical setting.
signs.question: What ancient or pre-social force underlies this milieu?

family.title: Watershed wildfire
family.note: Wildfire at night: raw element devouring the milieu.
family.flip: a figure appears whose body is seized by the fire's force

family.title: Airport America
family.note: A drowned dead forest: a swamp of pre-human force.
family.flip: the trees lose all menace: an emptied, neutral space

family.title: [Amateur film: "Frisco Fair / Pacific Northwest"]
family.note: A dark forest shot through with light: the forest world of Innocence.
family.flip: the forest's depth reads as pure space rather than primal force

family.title: General Health Habits
family.note: An isolated house under a black tree: the milieu gone primal.
family.flip: nothing primal remains: a disconnected, affective space

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: Figures on a jungle path: the forest swallowing a human procession.
family.flip: the people's task (travel, trade) defines the space

family.title: [Completion of Northwestern Pacific Rail Road] (Part I)
family.note: A tunnel mouth in raw rock: the depths of the world opening.
family.flip: the railway reads as working infrastructure, a determinate milieu

signs.name: Index of lack
signs.gloss: the situation is an ellipsis which is unequivocally revealed
signs.difference: Something is visibly missing from the situation (an ellipsis) and the character's action fills it in one unequivocal disclosure that then redirects what they do.
signs.question: What missing situation does this action let us infer?

family.title: Dating: Do's and Don'ts
family.note: A man at the door: the arrival implies a situation off-screen.
family.flip: the arrival could imply two different situations off-screen

family.title: All My Babies
family.note: An examination at a bedside: a look that infers what happened.
family.flip: the look belongs to a routine hospital milieu rather than disclosing a lack

family.title: Wreckless
family.note: A man entering a room: the door opens onto the missing situation.
family.flip: what he finds could support two incompatible situations

family.title: Victory Gardens
family.note: Hands digging into soil: an action unearths what was hidden.
family.flip: the digging is just gardening, with no hidden situation

family.title: The Money Story
family.note: A hand uncovering a shape in sand: the situation disclosed by a gesture.
family.flip: the drawn sign carries an idea (money) and discloses no situation: this reads more as symbol

family.title: Space Shuttle: A Remarkable Flying Machine
family.note: A circle of light in the dark: searching makes the scene appear.
family.flip: with no searcher shown, the light is only space and glow

signs.name: Index of equivocity
signs.gloss: the situation is revealed as ambiguous
signs.difference: An action discloses a situation that stays double: a slight difference in the same act refers it to two distant situations at once — 'this and that' — and the film sustains the undecidability.
signs.question: What two worlds could explain the same action?

family.title: All My Babies
family.note: An embrace that reads as comfort or as restraint.
family.flip: the grip hardens into open struggle between two poles

family.title: Key to Our Horizons
family.note: A hand at a lock: entering, or breaking in?
family.flip: the next shot settles it (key or crowbar) and the ambiguity closes

family.title: Fighter for Freedom: The Frederick Douglass Story
family.note: A man lifting a child: rescue or seizure.
family.flip: context resolves it (a parent, a kidnapper)

family.title: The Electric House
family.note: Two identical doors: two worlds behind one gesture.
family.flip: the doors become alternative pasts rather than two readings of one act

family.title: The Playhouse
family.note: A figure in a dark doorway: welcome or threat.
family.flip: no action is implied at all: only a dark, affective space

signs.name: Vector
signs.gloss: multiple situations within the homogeneous universe
signs.difference: Many characters each disclose a partial, equivocal situation, and only their interlocking over the film draws the broken, unpredictable but necessary line of one world.
signs.question: How do several incomplete situations compose a world?

family.title: Formations
family.note: Cars crossing an intersection from above: separate trajectories in one space.
family.flip: the traffic pattern reads as a habitual, repeating series

family.title: Scatter radar: Space research from the ground
family.note: A street market from above: each figure on its own errand.
family.flip: the market is one determinate milieu rather than many partial situations

family.title: Broadway Limited
family.note: Tracks braiding and splitting: the broken line whose path is unpredictable.
family.flip: the branches read as alternative, irreconcilable paths

family.title: Restaurant Operator, The
family.note: Cooks at separate stations: Ajami's interlocking, unrelated tasks.
family.flip: the kitchen reads as a single workplace milieu

family.title: Ant City
family.note: Ants each on its own route: many partial situations in one field.
family.flip: the ants stand in for a human society (a trope)

family.title: Trading Centers of the Pacific Coast
family.note: Trails crossing and recrossing: the record of many unfinished journeys.
family.flip: the lines read as a diagram of thought

signs.name: Milieu
signs.gloss: the situation explicated through character actions
signs.difference: The situation is given before anyone acts: an establishing or extreme wide shot lays out a determined geo-historical and social space, and the people in it exemplify it rather than change it.
signs.question: What world produces these actions?

family.title: Mechanical Engineering at duPont
family.note: An industrial town from above: the determinate world that will call for action.
family.flip: the town is emptied of function: space without its uses

family.title: Nature's Cameo: Bryce Canyon National Park
family.note: Cowboys driving cattle across open range: the western milieu and its tasks.
family.flip: the drive becomes a confrontation between herd and riders

family.title: How Our Country Grew
family.note: A dense town seen from the air: the milieu as an encompassing whole.
family.flip: the grid reads as a cerebral topology

family.title: This Is My Railroad (Part I)
family.note: A rail yard and signal tower: a world of working functions.
family.flip: the yard is deserted: a disconnected space

family.title: Letter From an Airline Pilot (Part I)
family.note: A lecturer before a classroom diagram: the social order explained, as in marxism today's GDR classroom.
family.flip: the diagram becomes the thinking space itself rather than an explanation of a world

family.title: Boulder Dam
family.note: Desert with yucca: the geography that shapes whoever enters it.
family.flip: the desert reads as primordial, pre-social force

signs.name: Binomial
signs.gloss: a whole world of duels
signs.difference: Two opposed lines of force, embodied in characters, face each other: the image is organised as a duel (violent, romantic, political) pointing toward a decisive confrontation.
signs.question: Where has the world become a duel?

family.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part VII)
family.note: Two teams at the line of scrimmage: the world polarised into sides.
family.flip: the game reads as a rehearsal of a real conflict

family.title: Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge Desert Wilderness
family.note: Two rams squaring off on a ridge: the duel in nature.
family.flip: the charge is drive, not a duel that structures a world

family.title: Working Together: A Case History in Labor-Management Cooperation
family.note: Labour and management face to face: the duel of Made in Dagenham.
family.flip: no side is taken: it is simply the workplace

family.title: We Learn About the Telephone I
family.note: Two cartoon figures eye to eye: the binomial as pure form.
family.flip: the animated duel is play rehearsing a conflict

family.title: De graal pinksterzegen
family.note: Two rows of figures facing each other: a ceremony of opposition.
family.flip: the rows are a ceremony of bodies, not a confrontation

signs.name: Imprint
signs.gloss: an indelible impression of the world upon a character
signs.difference: A complex situation has entered one body: the character carries it as visible, contained pressure, often fixed on an emotional object that links them to the world, before (or as) it bursts into action.
signs.question: How has the world gotten inside the character?

family.title: Twenty-Four Hours of Progress (Part II)
family.note: A hard-hatted worker, head bowed: labour written into the body.
family.flip: the fatigue is shown for its own sake, not as the world's imprint driving action

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: A bedridden woman holding a keepsake: the world pressed into an object.
family.flip: the keepsake triggers a flashback that decides what follows

family.title: Going Steady?
family.note: A young man brooding: the situation turned inward.
family.flip: the face becomes a pure affective surface with no world behind it

family.title: Ole' 23
family.note: A boy looking out at the school bus: the environment weighing on a small figure.
family.flip: the vehicle dwarfs him and his action counts for nothing

family.title: FIVE ARTISTS
family.note: A lone figure before a monumental facade: the building's order bearing down.
family.flip: the figure is simply tiny before the building

family.title: Consumers Want to Know (Part I)
family.note: A man by a turntable: like Fish Tank's record, the world held in a charged object.
family.flip: the sound from the machine becomes the situation itself

signs.name: Plastic figure
signs.gloss: small form transformed by the large form, an implied situation
signs.difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?
signs.question: What greater situation does this action unexpectedly imply?

family.title: Western Cattle Sequence
family.note: Cattle in the slaughter pens: the abattoir as trope for a massacre.
family.flip: the slaughter hardens into a stable symbol rather than a trope inside an action

family.title: [Chevrolet Sales Convention Musical]
family.note: A showroom song-and-dance number: spectacle swallows the everyday, as in The Wandering Cloud.
family.flip: the number rehearses a real action instead of enveloping one

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part III)
family.note: A line of posed bathing beauties: a staged spectacle wrapping an implied desire.
family.flip: the pose is a rehearsal rather than a trope

family.title: Coffee Break
family.note: An hourglass: a small object made to stand for a whole situation of time.
family.flip: the hourglass carries a concept (time) independent of any action

family.title: National Wildlife Refuge System
family.note: A wildlife stamp: a miniature standing in for a whole landscape.
family.flip: the miniature virtually contains the whole environment

signs.name: Theatrical figure
signs.gloss: a sequence of images as precursor of the real action
signs.difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?
signs.question: What real action is being rehearsed through fiction?

family.title: [San Francisco General Strike] (Part II)
family.note: A staged first-aid drill: rehearsing the real emergency.
family.flip: the drill discloses a real accident that happened

family.title: Sleep for Health
family.note: Two boys sparring: the fight rehearsed as play.
family.flip: the sparring turns into a real duel

family.title: The Snow Queen (Animation)
family.note: A cartoon battle: conflict rehearsed in animation, as in Scott Pilgrim.
family.flip: the animated world moves by itself: nothing is being rehearsed

family.title: Where the Sun Reigns
family.note: A massed drill: war performed before it is fought.
family.flip: the drill is a ceremony of bodies, not a rehearsal of a real act

family.title: Powers Music School Presents: Musical Story Hour 02/28/09
family.note: A school stage show under a skull banner: fiction dressing a threat.
family.flip: the show becomes an image inside the image, recursively

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 5) (Part I)
family.note: A puppet stage: a fictive action that prefigures the real.
family.flip: the stage nests one action-world inside another

signs.name: Mise en abyme
signs.gloss: a recurrence of plastic and theatrical figures
signs.difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?
signs.question: Is one action-world nested inside another?

family.title: Television Remote Control (Tuner)
family.note: A woman watching a television that shows another scene: an image within the image.
family.flip: the watcher is frozen before the screen: pure seeing

family.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHER
family.note: A photographer at his tripod: the film showing a picture being made.
family.flip: the camera marks the whole scene as staged

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A cameraman filming from a rig: the apparatus inside its own picture.
family.flip: the apparatus exposes the image as fabrication

family.title: 1959 RCA 21-inch TV Screen
family.note: A television set mid-broadcast: the screen doubled inside the screen.
family.flip: the broadcast is another present coexisting with this one

family.title: Let's Go To The Movies
family.note: An audience at the movies: cinema watching itself.
family.flip: the audience's shared affect matters more than the screen

signs.name: Figure of the sublime
signs.gloss: actions surpass the determinates of an enfeebled situation
signs.difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?
signs.question: Is the action bigger than the world requires?

family.title: The Balloonatic
family.note: Keaton's The Balloonatic: a visionary contraption, doomed.
family.flip: the whole world starts to move with dream logic

family.title: American Road, The (Part I)
family.note: A land yacht sailing the highway: the grand gesture exceeds the road.
family.flip: the yacht is a weekend hobby, not a crazy enterprise

family.title: Amateur Film - Little Journeys to Niagara
family.note: A giant wheeled contraption: the crazy enterprise built in hardware.
family.flip: the contraption is only an everyday machine

family.title: The Battling Kangaroo
family.note: A boxing kangaroo: a spectacle out of all proportion to its occasion.
family.flip: the bout is theatre, a staged act

family.title: Belo Horizonte
family.note: Earthworks carving a hillside: action bigger than the world asked for.
family.flip: the works are the ordinary transformation of a milieu

family.title: Auto-Lite on Parade
family.note: A massed parade in formation: spectacle swollen beyond its purpose.
family.flip: the formation is ceremony, not a visionary enterprise

signs.name: Figure of enfeeblement
signs.gloss: weak characters reveal the sublime nature of the world
signs.difference: Do a weak character's small, futile acts make an immense, indifferent world swell into view (the tiny point fleeing to the horizon), rather than the world merely sitting there?
signs.question: Is the actor tiny compared with the world disclosed?

family.title: Aqua Frolics
family.note: A small boat tossed in surf: the power belongs to the sea.
family.flip: the crew's struggle becomes a heroic overreach

family.title: Oil Across Arabia
family.note: A figure in the Arabian desert: the landscape outscales every act.
family.flip: the figure's task defines the desert as a working milieu

family.title: Amateur Film Children Playing Near Hudson
family.note: A man sitting idle in a garden chair: Slackistan's drift.
family.flip: the idle posture is the thought itself, not a revelation of the world's scale

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 1
family.note: People dwarfed by a ruined city: the disaster discloses the world's scale.
family.flip: the ruin empties out: space with no one in it

family.title: Heavenly Bodies
family.note: A small figure on an empty path: going nowhere across the frame.
family.flip: the walk is simply ordinary daily life

family.title: AUTOMOBILE ECONOMY TEST, ca. 1938
family.note: An empty sea horizon: the world vast, the actor almost absent.
family.flip: there is no actor at all: pure emptied space

signs.name: Quotidian
signs.gloss: everyday situations, everyday actions – sublime ↔ futile
signs.difference: Is an everyday act shown so that you cannot decide whether it is trivial or heroic, the situation both inconsequential and unfathomable at once?
signs.question: Has everyday life become both ridiculous and heroic?

family.title: Health: Your Posture
family.note: A woman at household chores: repetition, sublime and futile.
family.flip: the gesture is an attitude of the body rather than an everyday action

family.title: Inside/Outside: The Story of Food and Fitness
family.note: A couple eating at the kitchen table: the meal as a whole life.
family.flip: the bodies' fatigue and posture become the subject

family.title: Industry on Parade: Sylacauga Saga
family.note: A swimmer diving into a pool: A Screaming Man's pool, the everyday made grave.
family.flip: the dive becomes a feat, an action too big for the world

family.title: Century of Progress Exposition: Wings of a Century
family.note: A high dive against an empty sky: heroic and trivial in one movement.
family.flip: the dive reads as a sublime, excessive gesture

family.title: Story of a City: New York
family.note: Washing on a line: the most ordinary thing, patiently held.
family.flip: no one acts at all: a purely optical situation

family.title: Door to Heaven, The
family.note: A curtained room with a lamp: domestic space where nothing happens.
family.flip: nothing is done in the room: pure looking

signs.name: Limit of the large form action-image
signs.gloss: action explores a hidden problem
signs.difference: Before acting, does the character have to extract a question hidden in the situation (what is a samurai now?), so action is delayed into a considered response rather than an explosive reaction?
signs.question: What hidden question does this world contain?

family.title: Nieuwe stormramp in den Achterhoek
family.note: A house wrecked by flood: the situation no longer calls for action; it poses a question.
family.flip: the wreck reads as emptied space rather than a question the world poses

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: A column of people moving through jungle: an evacuation with no visible enemy.
family.flip: the procession has a clear task in a determinate milieu

family.title: Colaci Home Movies: Family 1952-1956 (Part I)
family.note: An adobe wall in empty desert: like the wall in Monsters, a boundary whose meaning is unclear.
family.flip: the wall is ordinary architecture in a determinate milieu

family.title: Indisch allerlei
family.note: A ruined wall overgrown by jungle: the hidden problem inside the milieu.
family.flip: the ruin reads as a primal world rather than a hidden problem

family.title: Airport America
family.note: A low plane over farmland: threat or routine?
family.flip: the plane is an aberration in a habitual series (Hitchcock's crop-duster)

signs.name: Limit of the small form action-image
signs.gloss: the situation revealed as a problem
signs.difference: Do parallel, heterogeneous lines of action connect only as pieces from different puzzles, so the situation they reveal remains an unanswered cipher, a sustained ellipsis?
signs.question: Why do the clues refuse to settle the situation?

family.title: Apollo 12: Pinpoint for Science
family.note: Hands fitting map pieces together: fragments that never close into a whole.
family.flip: the map becomes a diagram of thought in its own right

family.title: Principles of Electricity
family.note: Letter blocks scattered on a table: the clues stay heterogeneous.
family.flip: the letters demand to be read, not assembled

family.title: Arteries of New York City
family.note: Tenement fronts: like the projects in Brooklyn's Finest, a situation read in pieces.
family.flip: the housing is simply the milieu that produces action

family.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]
family.note: Two men in suits on a tenement street: plain-clothes watch, meaning withheld.
family.flip: their action points to two incompatible situations

family.title: Third Avenue El
family.note: The street seen from the elevated railway: partial evidence from above.
family.flip: the street holds many partial trajectories at once

signs.name: Limit of the action-image (extreme limit)
signs.gloss: a whole world of problems
signs.difference: Is the film permeated by problems from start to end so that you can no longer tell whether they are posed by the situation or discovered by action, the world itself appearing as a field of indeterminate forces?
signs.question: Has action itself stopped being an adequate solution?

family.title: Where the Bankers Bank
family.note: An armoured truck and its guard: Metro Manila's van, the job that has itself become the problem.
family.flip: the truck is ordinary infrastructure in a working milieu

family.title: Logic By Machine (Part II)
family.note: A man in profile beside a logic machine: thinking takes the place of acting.
family.flip: the machine becomes the brain-screen itself

family.title: Boulder Dam
family.note: A black hole blasted in rock: a cipher at the centre of the world.
family.flip: the hole is simply a disconnected, emptied space

family.title: Men, Steel and Earthquakes
family.note: Workers amid excavation rubble: a world of problems no single act resolves.
family.flip: the site is a determinate milieu of work

signs.name: Rich dream
signs.gloss: radically distinct real world and dream world
signs.difference: Is the passage into the dream explicitly marked and ornately made (dissolves, superimpositions, effects), with an equally marked exit, so the dream is attributed to a dreamer and recognised as dream by the viewer?
signs.question: Can we clearly tell when the dream begins?

family.title: Man of Action
family.note: A cartoon thought-cloud: the dream bubble, clearly bracketed off from waking.
family.flip: the whole world, not a bracketed bubble, starts to dream

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A distorted, stretched close-up: the image bends into dream.
family.flip: the distortion stays on a face as pure affect

family.title: What's It to You? (Part I)
family.note: A kaleidoscope: an optical sign announcing that we have entered another regime.
family.flip: no dreamer and no return: the pattern is simply acentred matter

family.title: How the Ear Functions
family.note: Glowing spheres floating in black: a dream space set clearly apart.
family.flip: the multiplied images read as mirrors face to face

family.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part V)
family.note: A smear of blurred motion: the device that marks the passage into dream.
family.flip: the blur is only a camera in flowing motion

signs.name: Restrained dream
signs.gloss: an ambiguity between real world and dream world
signs.difference: Is the dream entered by an invisible cut and made of concrete everyday things with one impossible unhinging, so that the film's task becomes deciding whether we are awake?
signs.question: Are we unsure whether waking has ended?

family.title: Programmer with Magic Memory: Another Newsmaker
family.note: A man dozing in an armchair: we can't tell when sleep began.
family.flip: the dozing is simply the everyday body's attitude

family.title: POTTERY, ca. 1926
family.note: A cup blurred at the edge of focus: the everyday slightly off.
family.flip: the blur is a marked optical device announcing a dream

family.title: Let Yourself Go
family.note: A woman opening a door onto darkness: an unmarked passage between worlds.
family.flip: the darkness reads as emptied space rather than a passage into dream

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A hand with a cigarette against black: an isolated detail oddly insisted upon.
family.flip: the cigarette becomes the charged object of a drive

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part II)
family.note: A dim window onto a blank wall: realism gone uncanny.
family.flip: the window is a purely optical situation with no dream at stake

family.title: Master Hands
family.note: A gaunt worker at a machine in low light: the lathe of The Machinist, waking life already dreamlike.
family.flip: the gauntness is the world's imprint driving an action

signs.name: Movement of world
signs.gloss: the dream world is the real world
signs.difference: Is there no entry or exit at all: does the world itself carry the character along (song, dance, impossible events treated as natural) so that no one is the dreamer?
signs.question: What if nobody ever wakes up?

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 1) (Part I)
family.note: A chorus line on a lit stage: the musical where the décor dances, Deleuze's movement of world.
family.flip: the dance reads as a ceremony of linked bodies

family.title: The Snow Queen (Animation)
family.note: A lantern floating through an animated night: a dream with no dreamer to wake.
family.flip: a dreamer is shown and the lantern belongs to their dream

family.title: Coney Island At Night (Standard 4:3)
family.note: Coney Island rides at night: the world itself spinning in light.
family.flip: the lights become acentred matter with no world to dream

family.title: Drive-in Intermission 6
family.note: An animated swirl: the setting animates itself.
family.flip: the swirl is a bracketed dream device with a way back out

family.title: Berlin: Symphony of a Great City
family.note: Berlin's city machine in motion: the world moves with dream logic.
family.flip: the blur is pure molecular motion rather than a dreaming world

family.title: Changing City, The
family.note: Skyscrapers slanting overhead: the city folding, as in Inception's Paris.
family.flip: the angle is only an establishing view of a city milieu

signs.name: Strong destiny
signs.gloss: a flashback to the past determines the future
signs.difference: Does a marked flashback (pause, dissolve, monochrome, reverb) return to the present and pass through affect into an action it determines, closing a causal circuit?
signs.question: Does the remembered past command what happens next?

family.title: Mirror of America
family.note: A bleached, overexposed march: the past visibly marked as past.
family.flip: the past is not a flashback that decides but a layer we move through

family.title: Farmer Miller Goes Into High Gear (Part II)
family.note: Hands holding old photographs: the recollection that will decide what happens.
family.flip: the photographs carry an idea rather than trigger a determining memory

family.title: Financial Investigation - Fundamentals
family.note: An older man in an armchair, lost in reverie: the moment before the flashback.
family.flip: no flashback follows: the face is pure affect

family.title: Singing Wires
family.note: A figure at a desk in lamplight: like the writer at the typewriter in The Secret in Their Eyes, the past pulling on the present.
family.flip: the writer's lamplit work is simply everyday life

family.title: Alcohol and the Human Body
family.note: A man lying back, eyes closed: memory about to take command.
family.flip: what follows is a dream, not a memory

signs.name: Weak destiny
signs.gloss: the content of the flashback permeates affects
signs.difference: Is the flashback ambiguous, incomplete or shared, so it saturates present feeling as a clue to an ellipsis that must be reconstructed before any action can follow?
signs.question: Does memory color the present without dictating it?

family.title: NEW ORLEANS, ca. 1923
family.note: An old, worn street scene: a fragment of the past that belongs to no one.
family.flip: the footage is itself a sheet of the past

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: A colonial house and its veranda: a history hanging over the present without explaining it.
family.flip: the house is a layer of the past we inhabit, not a colouring memory

family.title: Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge Desert Wilderness
family.note: A lone figure on a dirt road through dry land: Maria's road in White Material, the past colouring every step.
family.flip: the landscape simply dwarfs her

family.title: Plant Solutions Video - Mini
family.note: Figures walking through tall grass: transit through a landscape charged with the past.
family.flip: the walkers belong to a determinate working milieu

family.title: Golden Gate City
family.note: A crowded streetcar: bodies in transit, carrying histories no flashback explains.
family.flip: the streetcar is a city milieu and nothing more

family.title: Singing Wheels
family.note: A truck on a tree-lined road: movement suspended, destination uncertain.
family.flip: the road is one of several partial trajectories

signs.name: Forking paths
signs.gloss: a matrix of irresolvable flashbacks
signs.difference: Do flashbacks fork within flashbacks, irreconcilably, so the past is explored for its own sake as an inexplicable secret and psychological causality is shown to be a ruse?
signs.question: Which past, if any, actually explains the present?

family.title: Going Steady?
family.note: A boy and his image in a hand mirror: the self doubled, each image an alternative.
family.flip: the doubling is a mirror-image, not alternative pasts

family.title: Allegheny Portage Railroad
family.note: Tracks forking at a station: paths literally branching.
family.flip: the branches are a vector's broken line in the present, not pasts

family.title: Back-Room Boy
family.note: A boat half-lost in fog: which crossing is this?
family.flip: the fog empties space rather than splitting time

family.title: Health: Your Posture
family.note: Two faces mirroring each other: the double within one frame.
family.flip: the faces are mirror doubles, not incompatible pasts

family.title: Small Steps...Giant Strides
family.note: A lone figure on a beach at dusk: Triangle's shore, where the loop restarts.
family.flip: the beach is a purely optical situation with no loop implied

family.title: Oil Across Arabia
family.note: A ship alone at sea: Triangle's liner, the same voyage coming round again.
family.flip: the ship is just small on a vast sea

signs.name: Mark
signs.gloss: the relation between a habitual series of images
signs.difference: Can you point to at least three occurrences of the same image or motif that the characters or viewer come to read as one habitual series with a meaning to be deciphered?
signs.question: What recurring thing has become meaningful because it repeats?

family.title: Place to Live, A
family.note: Identical row houses: repetition makes the relation visible.
family.flip: the houses are simply a suburban milieu

family.title: According to Plan: The Story of Modern Sidewalls for the Homes of America
family.note: A planned street of matching houses: a pattern the viewer learns.
family.flip: the street is a milieu rather than a learned series

family.title: Big Train, The (Part I)
family.note: Glowing bulbs in a row: a series whose term is the single unit.
family.flip: the glow becomes acentred light rather than a countable series

family.title: White Ammunition
family.note: Rows of cartridges: the series as a habit of the eye.
family.flip: the series is serial copying without an original

family.title: Communications Primer, A
family.note: A printed list: Se7en's lists, the series written down.
family.flip: the list has to be read rather than seen as a series

family.title: Two Pay Days (Part I)
family.note: A clerk at his ledger: the habitual entry, one more in the series.
family.flip: the clerk's entry is ordinary daily work

signs.name: Demark
signs.gloss: an aberration in the series of habitual images
signs.difference: Does the shot show a known term of an established series appearing out of place or contradicting that series, so that the aberration itself shocks thought?
signs.question: What breaks the pattern?

family.title: Finding Your Life's Work
family.note: Rows of identical figures with one singled out: the aberration drawn as a diagram.
family.flip: no figure is singled out: the chart shows only a series

family.title: Crop Duster
family.note: A crop-duster low over a field: Deleuze's demark, a plane dusting where there are no crops (North by Northwest).
family.flip: the plane is simply doing its habitual job over a crop

family.title: Henry Ford's Mirror of America (Part II)
family.note: A line of marchers with one figure out of place.
family.flip: the out-of-place figure is just the leader of the column

family.title: Amateur Film Northwest
family.note: A flock with a stray: the series shows its rule by breaking it.
family.flip: the flock reads as a collective affect rather than a series with a break

family.title: Miss Clark Introduces Panorama
family.note: A windmill: Hitchcock's mill turning against the wind, the natural series broken (Foreign Correspondent).
family.flip: the mill stands for a country rather than breaking a series

family.title: Insects
family.note: A creature coiled where it should not be: the snake in Buried's coffin.
family.flip: the creature is a charged object rather than an aberration

signs.name: Symbol
signs.gloss: an object expressing ideas, beliefs, concepts
signs.difference: Is a single concrete object held on screen as the knot where several separate threads of the film's relations meet, so that it carries an idea, belief or concept rather than a use or a desire?
signs.question: What idea is being thought through this thing?

family.title: Learning to Set Type
family.note: A lighter held in the dark: Buried's flame, an object carrying the film's ideas.
family.flip: the flame stores primal energy rather than expressing an idea

family.title: Industries of the United States: Steel - The Hardest Metal in the World
family.note: A padlock and chain: bondage as an idea you can hold.
family.flip: the lock is charged with an impulse rather than a concept

family.title: 6 1/2 Magic Hours
family.note: A packed suitcase: departure thought through a thing.
family.flip: the suitcase is a relic charged with a person rather than an idea

family.title: Bookkeeping and You
family.note: A wristwatch in close-up: time as an object.
family.flip: the watch belongs to a habitual series of time-checks

family.title: Key to Our Horizons
family.note: A hand turning a key: Hitchcock's key, a relation made into an object.
family.flip: the gesture could be entry or burglary: an equivocal action

family.title: Let's Go To The Movies
family.note: A gramophone horn: voice and memory cast in brass.
family.flip: the sound it emits becomes the situation itself

signs.name: Opsign
signs.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure optical situation
signs.difference: With the sound off, is the image something to be seen and nothing more: no one's goal organises it, what moves in it resolves nothing, and the look is not converted into action?
signs.question: Can this sight still be discharged into action?

family.title: Alice In Wonderland
family.note: A figure small on a sepia beach: Five's shoreline, a purely optical situation.
family.flip: no one is there to see: the beach is only a disconnected space

family.title: Alaska's Silver Millions (Part I)
family.note: A lone figure on a snowfield: action has stalled into looking.
family.flip: the figure's smallness before the snow is the point

family.title: Panama by Air (Reel 4)
family.note: Haze over the sea: a seeing that has nowhere to go.
family.flip: the haze reads as amorphous space rather than a seeing cut off from action

family.title: Legacy for Wings
family.note: An old man looking out over wetland: the seer who no longer acts.
family.flip: the face becomes an affective surface rather than a seer

family.title: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: A still marsh: duration with nothing to do.
family.flip: the marsh is space for its own sake with no seer implied

family.title: Autoraces op boulevard Scheveningen
family.note: A seaside promenade with walkers crossing: Five's jetty, events without a plot.
family.flip: the promenade is ordinary daily life, patiently held

signs.name: Sonsign
signs.gloss: the zeroness of the time-image: a pure sound situation
signs.difference: With the image covered, does a sound hold the scene as a situation in itself, not score, not plot-driving dialogue, not a cue someone answers?
signs.question: Does this sound stand alone as a situation, answered by no action?

family.title: Valley Town
family.note: A factory whistle on the roofline: the sound is the situation, and no worker is shown answering it. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound: low tonal hum, no speech.
family.flip: the whistle calls workers to action: sound in the service of a milieu

family.title: Command Performance
family.note: A record turning on a phonograph in an empty room: sound on its own. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound, no speech rhythm.
family.flip: the gramophone stands for an idea (memory, modernity) rather than being heard

family.title: Uruguay
family.note: People in a square beneath a loudspeaker pole: a sound situation no one answers. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound, steady, no speech rhythm.
family.flip: the soundtrack turns out to be narration or score: only the optical situation remains

family.title: Muscatatuck National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: A pond at dusk, frogs and birds: Five's toads, sound without an action attached. Audio analysis (heuristic): tonal: likely music score.
family.flip: the track is music scoring (tonal audio detected): the pond is only optical

family.title: Communications and Our Town
family.note: A church belfry: bells heard over a town with no one moving. Audio analysis (heuristic): speech: likely narration.
family.flip: the track is narration (speech detected): the belfry signifies community rather than being heard

family.title: Party Magic (Beich Screen Ad--"Whiz" Bar)
family.note: A family gathered still around the radio: hearing replaces doing. Audio analysis (heuristic): speech: likely narration.
family.flip: the track is narration (speech detected): listening is just the family's routine, and the voice drives the film

signs.name: Mirrors face to face
signs.gloss: fragments, duplicates and distortions
signs.difference: Does one body or thing appear in the same shot as several reflections or doubles at once (facing, angled or distorting mirrors, glass), so that actual and virtual can no longer be told apart?
signs.question: Which image is original?

family.title: Frigidaire Finale 1957
family.note: A woman at her mirror: the actual image and its virtual double, face to face.
family.flip: the reflection starts replacing the woman: actual and virtual swap

family.title: Day At The Fair, A
family.note: A funhouse distortion: the image multiplied and warped.
family.flip: the distortion is a marked device bracketing a dream

family.title: Barbers
family.note: A boy in the barber's mirror: the reflection returns the scene from another side.
family.flip: the mirror is just part of an ordinary barbershop

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: A man beside his reflection: two images, neither simply first, as in Black Swan's mirrors.
family.flip: the second image is a representation nested inside the scene

family.title: Alchemist In Hollywood, The (Part II)
family.note: A strip of repeated frames: duplicates with no original.
family.flip: the repeated frames are a habitual series

family.title: Small Steps...Giant Strides
family.note: A faceted reflecting structure: fragments of one world across many planes.
family.flip: the facets read as acentred matter rather than doubled images

signs.name: Limpid and opaque
signs.gloss: the exchange of the actual and virtual
signs.difference: During the shot or scene, does one face of the image clear (becomes visible or real) while the other clouds (becomes obscure or virtual), so that the two sides keep changing places?
signs.question: Which side of the image is becoming real?

family.title: Industry on Parade: Outgoing Cargo, Workhorses of the Harbor, Refresher Course
family.note: A figure behind a translucent screen: seen and unseen at once.
family.flip: the screen merely doubles the figure as a reflection

family.title: Under Western Stars
family.note: Figures before a projected image: the real and its image changing sides.
family.flip: the projection is a film inside the film

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 3) (Part II)
family.note: A small stage, curtain parted: actor and role trading places, as in Self Made's workshop.
family.flip: the stage rehearses a real action rather than exchanging actual and virtual

family.title: Mastering Takeoffs and Landings
family.note: A face lit by a blue screen: the actual lit by the virtual.
family.flip: the screen he faces is an image nested inside the image

family.title: Dust Storm
family.note: A dust-hazed horizon: the visible sinking into the opaque.
family.flip: the haze is emptied space with nothing becoming visible or invisible

signs.name: Seed and environment
signs.gloss: (virtual/actual) seed ↔ (actual/virtual) environment
signs.difference: Is there a small enclosed image (a snow globe, model, miniature stage, a drop, a crystal) that contains in germ the world that surrounds it or will grow from it, with seed and environment reversible?
signs.question: What future world lies virtually inside this image?

family.title: Door to Heaven, The
family.note: A crystal cluster: the seed-crystal that could crystallise a whole environment.
family.flip: the crystal reads as acentred matter rather than the seed of a world

family.title: Have I Told You Lately That I Love You?
family.note: A miniature monument: a model world, like the city in a warehouse in Synecdoche, New York.
family.flip: the miniature nests one world inside another

family.title: Plant Solutions Video - Short
family.note: A sprouting seedling: a future environment folded into a seed.
family.flip: the sprout symbolises growth rather than containing a virtual environment

family.title: New World Through Chemistry
family.note: A glass model: a virtual world held in a small transparent thing.
family.flip: the glass doubles rather than crystallises

family.title: Unique Contribution, The (Part II)
family.note: A single red shoot: the germ before the milieu.
family.flip: the shoot stands for life as a concept

family.title: Wallops Island launch facility
family.note: A scale-model rocket: the seed of an environment still to be built.
family.flip: the model stands for an idea (progress)

signs.name: Peaks of the present
signs.gloss: the heterogeneous present
signs.difference: Does the narration give several different presents at once (a present of the past, a present of the present, a present of the future) in the same event, without flashback framing to rank them?
signs.question: What if several presents are simultaneously valid?

family.title: [First Private Atom Power Plant Opens]
family.note: A wall of clocks, each set to a different time: presents side by side.
family.flip: the clocks read as a habitual series of units

family.title: Finale
family.note: Tilted screens with different images: several nows at once.
family.flip: the screens are images nested inside the image

family.title: Introduction to Firearms
family.note: A blurred, ghostly figure: an impossible presence in the present, like Boonmee's ghost.
family.flip: the ghost belongs to a bracketed dream

family.title: Man and Space
family.note: Dials on a control panel: parallel times read at a glance.
family.flip: the dials are a series, not coexisting presents

family.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]
family.note: A framed picture on an easel: another present hung inside this one.
family.flip: the painting is an image inside the image

family.title: Hotel and Restaurant Workers
family.note: A laid dining table: Boonmee's dinner, where the dead sit down with the living.
family.flip: with no ghost at the table, it is simply a laid table

signs.name: Sheets of the past
signs.gloss: the non-chronological nature of the past
signs.difference: Does the film move between regions of the past that coexist and ricochet non-chronologically (layered periods in one space, without a present-day narrator motivating each return)?
signs.question: Which layer of the past are we inhabiting?

family.title: Miss Clark Introduces Panorama
family.note: A gallery of statues: pasts standing side by side.
family.flip: the gallery is a museum milieu and nothing more

family.title: Court to Court (Jun 2001)
family.note: A long arched corridor: a track through coexisting sheets of the past.
family.flip: the corridor is only a moving camera's route

family.title: This is Russia (Reel 2 of 2)
family.note: A palace interior: Russian Ark's Hermitage, rooms as layers of time.
family.flip: the room is a determinate milieu for action

family.title: Justice Depends on You: Working for the Federal Courts
family.note: A vaulted hall: architecture holding centuries at once.
family.flip: the hall is architecture in a determinate milieu

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 6
family.note: Ruins after the earthquake: a stratum laid bare.
family.flip: the ruin is emptied space rather than an exposed layer of time

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: Dancers in white: Russian Ark's last ball, a sheet of the past still turning.
family.flip: the dance is a ceremony of linked bodies rather than a sheet of the past

signs.name: Powers of the false
signs.gloss: serialism, the ongoing ungrounding of the image
signs.difference: Does the film expose its own claim to truth, with testimony, performance or versions that pass into one another so that no image can be held as the true one?
signs.question: What if contradiction generates rather than obstructs the story?

family.title: How Our Country Grew
family.note: Rows of identical model houses: serialism, the copy without an original.
family.flip: the copies are a habitual series rather than falsification

family.title: Thanksgiving Cooking Class 11/20/20
family.note: A woman speaking straight to camera: 24 City's testimony, where witness and actor can't be told apart.
family.flip: she is simply describing her day: testimony without falsification

family.title: From Trees to Tribunes (Part III)
family.note: Rows of identical workstations: 24 City's factory, repeated until it loses its ground.
family.flip: the rows are a series rather than an ungrounding of truth

family.title: RCA Presentation: Television, An
family.note: An audience in 3-D glasses: a crowd agreeing to a falsification.
family.flip: the audience's shared affect is the subject rather than the illusion

family.title: The Mission of Apollo / Soyuz, ca. 1975
family.note: A man talking to the lens at work: a witness whose truth is a performance.
family.flip: the talk is plain workplace documentary

signs.name: Bodies of attitude
signs.gloss: a dispersed individuation of the body
signs.difference: Is the body shown waiting, tired, slumped or posing, in its everydayness, with the posture itself as the content and no act prepared or completed?
signs.question: What does the body think before it acts?

family.title: Financial Investigation - Fundamentals
family.note: A man slumped back in his chair: the body's fatigue before any act.
family.flip: the slump is part of an everyday action rather than the body's own thinking

family.title: Alcohol and the Human Body
family.note: A man asleep in an armchair: the everyday body, all attitude.
family.flip: the sleep opens into a dream

family.title: Back of the Mike
family.note: A man sitting alone on rocks: waiting that isn't going anywhere.
family.flip: the rocks dwarf him and reveal the world's scale

family.title: Out West
family.note: A figure lying on a boxcar: the drifting rider of I'm Not There.
family.flip: the rider is simply tiny against the landscape

family.title: Japan
family.note: A body curled in rest: posture as thought.
family.flip: the posture is ritual, linked to others into a ceremony

family.title: Toute La Bande, Episode 9: Bricolage
family.note: A woman repeating a kitchen chore: habit inscribed in the body.
family.flip: the chore is an everyday action, not an attitude of the body

signs.name: Bodies of gest
signs.gloss: the linkage of attitudes creating differentiation
signs.difference: Are postures chained into a visible, repeated or staged gesture that performs a social act (ritual, bureaucratic routine, demonstration) and is shown as performance, not as efficient action?
signs.question: How do postures become social relations?

family.title: The Mission of Apollo / Soyuz, ca. 1975
family.note: Dignitaries in a row: posture as rank.
family.flip: the row is simply the setting of an official event

family.title: [Amateur film: Parade of Krewe of Rex, New Orleans, February 25, 1941]
family.note: Children in costume at a parade: attitudes linked into ceremony.
family.flip: the costumes perform a fiction that prefigures something real

family.title: Fire and Police Service
family.note: Firemen in a line with hoses: gesture drilled into a social choreography.
family.flip: the drill rehearses a real emergency

family.title: Structure Protection Strategies in the Wildland/Urban Interface
family.note: Three policemen standing for the camera: bodies arranged by the institution.
family.flip: each officer's individual attitude outweighs their arrangement

family.title: Bookkeeping and Accounting
family.note: An official reading from a large book: Police, Adjective's dictionary scene, meaning fixed by ceremony.
family.flip: the book's text has to be read rather than performed

family.title: Surviving Forced Landings
family.note: A hand-drawn diagram: the chief's blackboard, procedure turned into gesture.
family.flip: the diagram is the screen as cerebral space, with no body in it

signs.name: Cinema of the brain
signs.gloss: the screen as a cerebral space
signs.difference: Is the set or world laid out as a map of thought (abstract floor plans, chalk-drawn spaces, landscapes as mental states), so that the screen reads as a brain rather than a place to act in?
signs.question: Has the screen itself become a thinking system?

family.title: Banks And Credits
family.note: A town plan seen from above: like Dogville's chalk-drawn village, the world as a diagram of thought.
family.flip: the plan explains a determinate social milieu

family.title: Arteries of New York City
family.note: Branching lines across a dark field: arteries that read as neurons.
family.flip: the lines are acentred matter rather than thought

family.title: Growth of Cities
family.note: A growing street network: a city laid out like a cortex.
family.flip: the network is a city's milieu rather than a brain-space

family.title: Heat Treatment of Aluminum, Part I
family.note: A polygonal cell network: matter organised like tissue.
family.flip: the cells are gaseous matter with no cerebral topology

family.title: Caught Mapping
family.note: A hand drawing a map: space thought as it's made.
family.flip: the drawing is a clue in an unresolved situation

family.title: The Eclipse
family.note: A field of stars: the identity of cosmos and brain that Deleuze names.
family.flip: the stars are cosmos without any brain-identity

signs.name: Lectosigns
signs.gloss: the infinite of the time-image
signs.difference: Does grasping the film require you to relink its images, narration and narrative yourself, because none of them links 'naturally' and no single key object resolves it?
signs.question: What must I read here that I cannot simply see?

family.title: How Man Made Day
family.note: Neon signs at night: Enter the Void's Tokyo, light that has to be deciphered.
family.flip: the lights are an any-space-whatever of the city at night

family.title: Communications Primer, A
family.note: A page of text in the frame: reading replaces looking.
family.flip: the page expresses a single concept

family.title: Your Movie Camera and How to Use It
family.note: A page of printed instructions: the image must be read, not simply seen.
family.flip: the text carries one idea rather than demanding interpretation

family.title: Gift of Green
family.note: A glowing flower against black: an organic form that looks like something else.
family.flip: the flower is acentred matter rather than a form to be read

family.title: Ask Me, Don't Tell Me
family.note: A storefront of lettering: the street as text.
family.flip: the signs are simply part of the street milieu

family.title: Great American Chocolate Factory, The
family.note: Rows of red cones in close-up: an abstraction the eye can't settle.
family.flip: the cones are pure pattern rather than a legible image

films.title: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT

beats.title: Dim bedroom; Poet reads to an averted Ex

b.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]

beats.edit: Begin on the room; withhold the Ex's reverse angle. The next facade makes this intimacy spatially unreachable.
beats.operation: Bind the room to the Poet’s sightline; hold the Ex’s back as an unavailable reverse shot.
beats.gap: Shoot the named performers; source room, window and light plates.

beats.title: Ex on the fire escape

a.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]

beats.edit: Put the facade beside the bedroom for the final third; their mismatched scale makes separation visible.
beats.operation: Keep the distant body small within the building; enfeeblement requires more than small scale.
beats.gap: Back-facing Ex and the high-rise geography need continuity.

beats.title: Television showing world chaos

a.title: Hillsborough with New Hideaway Styling, The

beats.edit: Place chaos inside a clearly bounded television-shaped inset; enlarge the inset only after the room is established.
beats.operation: Nest the news image within the bedroom; a single screen is only a first layer of mise en abyme.
beats.gap: Composite selected news-like fragments into a television; do not label nesting alone recursive.

beats.title: Vapour erases the room
beats.edit: Let coastal fog replace the domestic image from halfway through; carry this fog motif to the later shore.
beats.operation: Let spatial coordinates dissolve, then hold the lost orientation without immediate action.
beats.gap: Vape origin, actor and room require a composite; generic smoke is a plate.

beats.title: Window approaches while Ex recedes

b.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]

beats.edit: Keep the building small while the room enlarges; this study tests incompatible distances without claiming a real dolly effect.
beats.operation: Change perceived distance without resolving the camera’s approach; an ambiguous dream transition can begin here.
beats.gap: Impossible recession needs camera choreography or compositing.

beats.title: Ex falls, Poet follows into clouds
beats.edit: Alternate falling-body reference and clouds, then finish with clouds alone; do not show a substitute Ex's face.
beats.operation: Use a marked fall as the threshold into a dream-world, then decide whether any secure waking exterior survives.
beats.gap: Two identifiable bodies and no visible Ex face require original or composited figures.

beats.title: Black and title card
beats.edit: Suspend the picture on black and the title. Let the continuous suite audio determine whether the interval opens a sonic situation.
beats.operation: Use black as an interval in which the poem or breath persists independently; literal title reading alone is not a lectosign.
beats.gap: Build the exact title card; sound relation must be designed.

beats.title: World chaos interrupts the fall

b.title: Hillsborough with New Hideaway Styling, The

beats.edit: Cut heterogeneous disasters against the earlier television cabinet; the world's scale now exceeds its domestic container.
beats.operation: Let heterogeneous scales disrupt the privileged perceiver; crisis is an assembly relation, not disaster imagery alone.
beats.gap: Select several fragments; preserve the distinction between historic footage and fictional world.

beats.title: Escapism: drugs and intoxication

b.title: Have I Told You Lately That I Love You?

beats.edit: Isolate a cigarette or drink against a larger apparatus of repetition; test compulsion through recurrence, not intoxication alone.
beats.operation: Test whether a drive overpowers the body and attaches to a partial object; consumption alone is insufficient.
beats.gap: Avoid treating all drinking or smoking as evidence of compulsive impulse.

beats.title: Escapism: party, television and phone

b.title: Hillsborough with New Hideaway Styling, The

beats.edit: Cycle party, television, telephone; repeat the television long enough to establish the escape series.
beats.operation: Build a recurring escape pattern so that its later interruption has an established series to break.
beats.gap: Modern phone use may require new footage; archival telephones are period substitutes.

beats.title: Crash into the vintage party
beats.edit: Land hard in the party after the fall. Give the new floor and collective movement time to establish a milieu.
beats.operation: Make the shift from falling to ballroom unmistakable; the party supplies a new determinate milieu.
beats.gap: Crash transition and actor insertion need effects; retain vintage party texture.

beats.title: Romantic slow motion and light leaks
beats.edit: Compare two dance-floor framings side by side; replacement moving footage should slow one stream while the other continues.
beats.operation: Alternate collective intensity with distinct faces; slow motion alone does not create a dividual.
beats.gap: Speed and light-leak treatment can be added editorially.

beats.title: Chase Ex through the crowd
beats.edit: Insert the receding passage into the party; the pursuit inherits the impossible bedroom distance.
beats.operation: Build a trajectory through partial spaces; use a misrecognised back only if it genuinely supports two situations.
beats.gap: Maintain Ex’s back and disappearance; do not invent a face match.

beats.title: Photographs, film and fiction as memory inserts

b.title: Belmont Historical Society Presents: Richard Betts Remembers 01/05/06

beats.edit: Interrupt the pursuit with still-photo textures; return to the party without presenting these as verified personal memories.
beats.operation: Let images solicit memory without prematurely fixing its causal meaning; old photographs alone are not sheets of past.
beats.gap: Optional insert from poem column; distinguish from the right-column staging.

beats.title: Floor opens; Poet falls into black
beats.edit: Drop the party into darkness. The eventual filmed body fall should end where the next suspended image begins.
beats.operation: Break the party’s geography through an impossible passage; action loses its stable environment.
beats.gap: Actor-specific fall and hole require a composite.

beats.title: Poet floats in black under flashes
beats.edit: Hold the suspended-body reference against black; keep the frame still enough for the absence of support to register.
beats.operation: Suspend the body in a field without practical coordinates; hold the optical situation beyond a response.
beats.gap: Black-space floating needs effects; retrieved flashes are lighting material.

beats.title: Unreachable Ex in distress

a.title: Selected scenes of past and present sport personalities - Part 1

b.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]

beats.edit: Repeat the distant figure/facade relation as an unreachable second panel; physical continuity remains an original-performance task.
beats.operation: Let an intensive face or bodily reach fail to become effective contact; keep the Ex’s face hidden.
beats.gap: Use Poet’s face for icon; do not violate the Ex’s back-only rule.

beats.title: Dilating eyes in darkness

a.title: Eyes and Their Care (An Introduction), The

b.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part I)

beats.edit: Magnify the eye over the childhood field; let the eye disappear before the memory gains a full frame.
beats.operation: Move from facial intensity into a subjective aperture; the close-up and POV perform different operations.
beats.gap: Pupil dilation and passage through the eye may require macro footage and effects.

beats.title: Enter childhood through the eye

a.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part I)

beats.edit: Move from the eye into the car environment with one slow dissolve; this is a marked memory threshold.
beats.operation: Use the eye transition to actualise a past; determine whether it explains or merely complicates present grief.
beats.gap: Matching child performer and eye transition require original work.

beats.title: Young Poet watches headlights sweep the room
beats.edit: Alternate headlights and the child/car reference without supplying a collision; light becomes a remembered threat.
beats.operation: Bind the light to the child’s viewpoint; an imprint requires accumulated pressure and later behavioural consequence.
beats.gap: Night window and moving headlights can be assembled from separate plates.

beats.title: Parents argue inside a parked car
beats.edit: Hold the car interior beside the exterior light. Conflict must come from staging or voice, not unrelated faces inferred as parents.
beats.operation: Stage two opposed lines of force, then expose the question the child cannot answer.
beats.gap: Relationship and location must be inferred from sequence, not facial tension alone.

beats.title: Ghost child appears, embraces Poet

b.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part I)

beats.edit: Bring back the childhood plate, then fade it out over the same field; the ghost requires a separate original figure layer.
beats.operation: Place an actual child and virtual visitor in a circuit; a superimposition alone does not establish indiscernibility.
beats.gap: Ghost performer and embrace need a controlled composite. Preserve the ghost’s disappearance as well as its appearance, embrace and prop exchange.

beats.title: Ghost gives the tambourine
beats.edit: Treat the prop as a small charged center before release. A placeholder object is not evidence of a tambourine handoff.
beats.operation: Make the instrument gather relational meaning; fetish remains conditional on an impulse stored in it.
beats.gap: Exact prop and exchange are likely an original insert.

beats.title: Tambourine through the window
beats.edit: Make the release-to-flight splice abrupt; match the prop position when original material is available.
beats.operation: Let the thrown object disclose the intolerable situation; establish the preceding pressure if reading it as imprint.
beats.gap: Throw, shatter and matching tambourine require a practical or effects insert.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Tambourine tumbles in black
beats.edit: Alternate prop-flight references with glazing and exterior distance; a sound bridge can carry one continuous fall across them.
beats.operation: Carry the object through discontinuous worlds; repeated returns can establish its habitual relation.
beats.gap: Isolated rotating prop over black is a planned effects shot.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Object enters chapel through intact window
beats.edit: Hold the window as a bounded aperture over the chapel; replace this geometric study with the intact-window passage.
beats.operation: Preserve the uncertain relation between broken and intact glass; it is equivocal only if both situations remain viable.
beats.gap: Composite the tambourine and intact window transition.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Empty chapel: pews, choir, baptism pool
beats.edit: Hold empty pews after the prop's motion; the change from trajectory to duration is the operative break.
beats.operation: Empty the social function of each space; hold the optical duration rather than merely establish a location.
beats.gap: Multiple interiors may require a constructed geography.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Accelerated chapel decay
beats.edit: Dissolve intact interior into roofless stone, keeping one central axis; the building decays before the shore is disclosed.
beats.operation: Measure construction and erosion against human action; time-lapse itself is not a chronosign.
beats.gap: No exact matched decay is presumed; use ruin plates plus staged or procedural decay.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Thunderstorm consumes the chapel
beats.edit: Give storm and ruin equal panels; neither weather footage nor masonry alone supplies the transformation.
beats.operation: Give the storm an independent acoustic duration; originary world requires forces beneath a social milieu, not weather alone.
beats.gap: Storm sound must be auditioned separately; destruction needs compositing.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Storm clears onto shoreline ruins
beats.edit: Let the shore occupy the whole image after the architectural fragments; hold beyond the arrival information.
beats.operation: Keep the aftermath as an unresolved optical situation before the next task begins.
beats.gap: An exact chapel-on-shore setting may need a composite.

beats.sequence: How to break off an engagement
beats.title: Tambourine lands and shatters

a.title: Astronauts: United States Project Mercury, ca. 1960

beats.edit: Repeat the earlier glass/prop material in sharper fragments; the repetition closes the engagement's object trajectory.
beats.operation: Break the recurring object’s established integrity; its symbolic relation must survive across appearances.
beats.gap: Original prop break or effects insert needed.

beats.title: Heartless Poet surveys the shore
beats.edit: Reduce the solitary figure against the shore; do not infer heartlessness from a stranger's expression.
